name: Pocket Worlds
description: Three tiny afternoons in an original hinged case. Open a harbor, a little town or a secret garden, then discover the mechanisms tucked inside.
compatibility: WebGL2 is required for the 3D scene. Unsupported devices receive a clearly labeled static illustration and the world descriptions.
Mouse/trackpad dragging, keyboard rotation and zoom, native vertical touch scrolling, labeled mechanism buttons and projected hotspots.
The case begins closed. Motion requires an action. Reduced motion makes transitions immediate; the open and mechanism sliders still support intermediate inspection.
Static geometry is instanced by shared geometry/material, while mechanism pivots retain their own local transforms. Rendering stops at rest, offscreen or when paused.
Shadows use one bounded 1024px directional map, with a capped device-pixel ratio. The effect is excluded from simultaneous comparison.
notes: Original molded shell, medallion, landscapes and mechanisms. The requested route is an identifier; this study is not affiliated with or a reproduction of a branded toy.
The cover rotates around a genuine rear hinge. Both shell halves have depth and recessed cavities; the closed interior contains the miniature pieces.
Each world has its own three mechanisms: a drawbridge/boat/keepsake box, a tram/fountain/post office, or a flower/roundabout/hidden sprout. Their transforms are sampled from normalized progress.
Hotspots project from 3D anchors and are hidden when occluded. Matching HTML action buttons remain available for touch and keyboard use.
Enter-world mode follows a gentle guided route above the miniature scenery, not an unrestricted first-person game. The exterior camera stays upright.
reuse: The complete exported example runs over local HTTP with bundled Three.js and its MIT license; no CDN or build step.
Use createPocketViewer(canvas, settings, definitions, builders) for a custom collection, or mount(host, settings) for the full experience.
World definitions separate shell dimensions, pieces, paths, camera routes and mechanisms. Custom geometry builders receive the shared kit and can reuse the same engine.
README.md documents schemas, pivot conventions, animation state, integration, accessibility, export and cleanup.
